subject.title: [Bug] Agent automatically executes config commands from example code without user confirmation

question: Should model-initiated OpenClaw self-management commands such as config writes, provider/model-default changes, gateway restarts, updates, or uninstall commands require explicit confirmation even when host exec is configured as full/off?
rationale: Source inspection proves the current gap, but the permanent rule changes OpenClaw’s documented trusted-operator exec boundary and could affect intentional automation.

options.title: Require self-management confirmation
options.body: Add a deterministic guarded class for OpenClaw config, provider/model, gateway lifecycle, update, and uninstall commands while leaving ordinary full/off host exec semantics intact.

options.title: Fold into broad confirmation gate
options.body: Keep this issue as a concrete scenario and implement the boundary through the broader response-level confirmation design at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/23451.

options.title: Keep full/off unchanged
options.body: Document that operators must opt into stricter exec approvals or sandboxing and accept raw exec self-management commands as trusted automation.

recommendation.title: Require self-management confirmation
recommendation.body: Add a deterministic guarded class for OpenClaw config, provider/model, gateway lifecycle, update, and uninstall commands while leaving ordinary full/off host exec semantics intact.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans security defaults, exec policy, and product compatibility, and prior review already routed the decision through core product/security design.
